title: How the Digestive System Works
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a bathroom-stall anecdote, then walk through how the digestive system works by following a ham sandwich from mouth to anus: saliva and amylase, swallowing and the epiglottis, peristalsis and the esophageal sphincters, stomach acid and mucus, chyme and the duodenum, jejunum and ileum absorption via villi and microvilli, the large intestine and gut bacteria, and the liver, gallbladder, and pancreas. They cover hormones (gastrin, CCK, PYY, ghrelin), nerves, how carbs, proteins, and vitamins are processed, and common problems: heartburn/GERD, ulcers and H. pylori, lactose intolerance, IBD and IBS, constipation, diarrhea, and gas. The episode ends with Kiva listener mail and a call for listeners to join the Stuff You Should Know Kiva team.

segments.title: Bathroom stall etiquette and episode intro
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about people sitting in the stall next to an occupied stall, then introduce the digestive system topic and a HowStuffWorks article.

segments.title: Digestive system overview and ham sandwich journey begins
segments.summary: The hosts note the digestive tract is about thirty feet long and the small intestine's surface area is the size of a tennis court. They begin following a ham sandwich, from smelling it to salivation and amylase in saliva.

segments.title: Swallowing, epiglottis, and the esophagus
segments.summary: Chewed food becomes bolus. The epiglottis guides food into the esophagus rather than the trachea. Peristalsis moves food down through the esophagus, past the upper and lower esophageal sphincters into the stomach. Heartburn and GERD are linked to a lazy lower esophageal sphincter.

segments.title: Stomach, mucus, and stomach growling
segments.summary: The stomach produces enzymes and acid and protective mucus; without mucus, acid can cause ulcers. Stomach growling is digestive contraction, triggered by hunger signals from the brain.

segments.title: Chyme, emptying the stomach, and the duodenum
segments.summary: Liquefied food, called chyme, leaves the stomach in about twenty minutes, while more solid material takes about an hour. The small intestine is divided into the duodenum, jejunum, and ileum, with the duodenum receiving enzymes from the pancreas and liver.

segments.title: Nutrient absorption through villi and microvilli
segments.summary: The hosts describe how the small intestine's folds, villi, and microvilli absorb specific nutrients into the bloodstream, after enzymes from the liver and pancreas break food down.

segments.title: Large intestine, water absorption, and gut bacteria
segments.summary: The large intestine absorbs fluid and salts and prepares solid waste. Gut bacteria ferment fiber. Fecal transplants are mentioned as a treatment for those who lose healthy bacteria. Waste moves about a centimeter per hour.

segments.title: Liver, gallbladder, pancreas, and hormones
segments.summary: The liver makes bile, stored in the gallbladder, and the pancreas makes enzymes. The hosts describe hormones gastrin, CCK, and the hunger and fullness hormones ghrelin and PYY, and the roles of nerves, including the vagus-related acetylcholine and adrenaline effects.

segments.title: Carbs, protein, and vitamins
segments.summary: Carbohydrates break down into glucose for energy, proteins into amino acids, and vitamins are water soluble (B and C) or fat soluble (A, D, K), with fat-soluble vitamins stored in fat cells.

segments.title: Burping, vomiting, ulcers, H. pylori, and lactose intolerance
segments.summary: Normal burping is three or four times after a meal. Vomiting is discussed. Peptic ulcers are linked to H. pylori bacteria, and Barry Marshall drank a culture to prove it. The hosts discuss lactose intolerance and their earlier casein mistake.

segments.title: IBD, IBS, and Crohn's disease
segments.summary: Inflammatory bowel disease includes colitis and Crohn's disease and is structural. IBS is functional, with cramps and gas, and responds to stress, hormonal changes, and antibiotics. A proposed law about bathroom access for Crohn's patients is mentioned.

segments.title: Gas, constipation, diarrhea, and the Bristol stool scale
segments.summary: Gas is mostly methane, hydrogen, and carbon dioxide, with normal gas release ten to twenty-five times a day. Constipation and diarrhea are described, and the Bristol stool scale is mentioned as a stool-type chart.

segments.title: Kiva listener mail and team call
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Kiva microloans, the Stuff You Should Know Kiva team's loan total of over $750,000, and a goal of one million dollars. They invite listeners to join the team and provide contact information.
